headline: Sánchez, Phillies open series at Washington today
recap: The Phillies' most recent game was Sunday's 9-4 win over the Braves in Atlanta. Atlanta scored first when Drake Baldwin's sacrifice fly brought home Michael Harris II in the first. J.T. Realmuto's two-run homer, his 11th of the season, put Philadelphia ahead 2-1 in the second, scoring Brandon Marsh. Matt Olson's RBI single tied it at 2-2 in the seventh, scoring Harris II. The Phillies broke the game open with seven runs in the eighth: Alec Bohm's two-run double scored Trea Turner and Bryce Harper, Bryson Stott's single drove in Bohm, J.T. Realmuto's single scored Stott, Kyle Schwarber's two-run single brought home Bryan De La Cruz and Realmuto, and Trea Turner's single scored Justin Crawford to make it 9-2. Matt Olson answered with a two-run homer, his 39th, in the bottom of the ninth to make it 9-4, the final score. Andrew Painter started and allowed one earned run over five innings; José Alvarado, who gave up Atlanta's tying run in the seventh, was credited with the win, and Tanner Banks worked the final two innings. Dylan Lee took the loss for Atlanta.
The Phillies are 83-67, second in the NL East, 4.5 games behind the division-leading Braves, and carry a one-game winning streak.

Philadelphia was off Monday and is at Washington today for the first of a two-game series at Nationals Park, with first pitch scheduled for 6:45 PM ET. Cristopher Sánchez starts for the Phillies opposite Jackson Kent for the Nationals; DraftKings lists the Phillies as -223 favorites.
